title: Angle types card
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Geometric notation and constructions; geometric reasoning
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lesson 53 (Angle types card (printable, in the pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 53: Naming angles and types of angle. To understand how to name angles with three letters and classify them by size

questions.model: Compare each with 90° and 180°. 35 < 90: acute. 90 < 125 < 180: obtuse. 270 > 180: reflex. 90 exactly: right angle.

questions.q: In triangle XYZ, which letter is the vertex of angle XZY?
One angle at a point is 70°. What is the reflex angle on the other side?
(a) Classify 12°, 89°, 91°, 179°, 181° and 300°. (b) A clock shows 3 o'clock: what angle is between the hands, and what type? (c) Name the vertex of angle DEF and of angle FED.
questions.a: (a) acute, acute, obtuse, obtuse, reflex, reflex (b) 90°, a right angle (c) E both times
questions.model: (a) The boundaries are 90° and 180°: 89 is just acute, 91 just obtuse, 181 just reflex. (b) Each hour is 360 ÷ 12 = 30°; 3 hours make 90°. (c) The middle letter both times: E.

questions.q: What angles do the hands make at 5 o'clock? Give the smaller angle and the reflex angle.
At 2:30 the hour hand is halfway between 2 and 3. Find the smaller angle between the hands.
questions.a: 105°: minute hand at 180°, hour hand at 2.5 × 30 = 75°, 180 - 75 = 105

questions.q: What is the vertex of angle PQR?
Big question: how can three letters name exactly one angle?
questions.a: The middle letter is the vertex and the outer letters show the two arms, so only one angle fits.
